story: The Senate passed H.R. 2347, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, 62 to 33 on November 19th with both Alaska senators yea; it names Alaska once, in a transmission subsection that gives the Regulatory Commission of Alaska an approval step, and adds a data center cost floor states may enforce

repeat_reasons: S. 5653 page incomplete at 100,000 characters, two offset repeats to reach the covered load definition
Petroleum News first response lacked the dated passage, one targeted repeat

claims.claim: Senate roll call vote 257 on November 9th invoked cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347 by 73 votes to 25.
claims.verbatim: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to H.R. 2347 ... On Cloture on the Motion to Proceed ... Agreed to ... 73 ... 25
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate, roll call vote menu, 119th Congress, 2nd session
claims.notes: Vote 00257, dated 09-Nov. The menu still describes H.R. 2347 by its original shell-bill subject; the Senate used it as the vehicle for the energy substitute. Corroborated by AP via OPB (C10).

claims.claim: Senate roll call vote 264 on November 16th invoked cloture on Capito Amendment No. 6883, a substitute amendment to H.R. 2347, by 70 votes to 27.
claims.verbatim: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Capito Amdt. No. 6883; In the nature of a substitute. ... On the Cloture Motion ... Agreed to
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate, roll call vote menu, 119th Congress, 2nd session
claims.notes: Vote 00264, dated 16-Nov, measure S.Amdt. 6883, 70 yeas and 27 nays.

claims.claim: Senate roll call vote 268 on November 18th invoked cloture on H.R. 2347 by 65 votes to 31.
claims.verbatim: Motion to Invoke Cloture Re. H.R. 2347 ... On the Cloture Motion ... Agreed to
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate, roll call vote menu, 119th Congress, 2nd session
claims.notes: Vote 00268, dated 18-Nov, 65 yeas and 31 nays.

claims.claim: Senate roll call vote 270 on November 19th passed H.R. 2347 as amended by 62 votes to 33.
claims.verbatim: H.R. 2347, as Amended ... On Passage of the Bill ... Passed
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate, roll call vote menu, 119th Congress, 2nd session
claims.notes: Vote 00270. Matches S01. Across the four votes support fell 73, 70, 65, 62.

claims.claim: NPR reported that the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act passed the Senate 62 to 33.
claims.verbatim: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, passed 62-33.
claims.source_outlet: NPR (Kate Bartlett), republished by Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: The article does not mention Murkowski or Sullivan; their votes rest on S02 and S03.

claims.claim: Fourteen Democrats and one independent joined most Republicans in supporting the bill.
claims.verbatim: Fourteen Democrats and one Independent joined most Republicans in supporting the bill.
claims.source_outlet: NPR (Kate Bartlett), republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: Sen. Jeff Merkley said the bill "opens the gates to a flood of natural gas for data centers."

claims.source_outlet: NPR (Kate Bartlett), republished by Alaska Public Media

claims.claim: S. 5653 as introduced defined covered load as data center electric load that equals or exceeds 20 megawatts, or is reasonably expected to reach 20 megawatts at full buildout.
claims.verbatim: (B) equals or exceeds 20 megawatts or, in the case of data centers or high-density computing facilities developed in phases, is reasonably expected to equal or exceed 20 megawatts at full buildout.

claims.notes: Introduced version only. The Senate-passed section 229 has no megawatt threshold (S21).

claims.claim: The North Slope data center would not be tied into the Railbelt electrical grid.

claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)
claims.notes: Single source; a recommendation to the Assembly.

claims.claim: The commission extended the mayor's proposed 12-month moratorium to 18 months.
claims.verbatim: extending the mayor's proposed 12-month timeframe to 18
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)
claims.notes: Single source.

claims.claim: The commission lengthened the administration's research deadline from six months to 10 months.
claims.verbatim: from six months to 10
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (Alex Bengel)
claims.notes: Single source.

claims.claim: Hopkins said the Borough Assembly vote will likely take place on January 14th.
claims.verbatim: a vote will likely take place on Jan. 14

claims.claim: Hopkins said "If it comes in as purely for a government purpose, I believe that would be not subject to our moratorium."

claims.verbatim: We're doing some research into that and trying to figure out how to turn that gray area black and white.

claims.source_outlet: Petroleum News (Kay Cashman)
claims.notes: Single trade-press source.

claims.claim: BlueCrest's plan is designed to achieve first Tyonek gas production on or before March 31st, 2027.
claims.verbatim: designed to achieve first Tyonek gas production on or before March 31, 2027
claims.source_outlet: Petroleum News (Kay Cashman)
claims.notes: A target.

claims.claim: On September 10th, BlueCrest executed a joint development agreement and drilling facility credit agreement with NBS Holding LLC.
claims.verbatim: On Sept. 10, 2026, BlueCrest executed a joint development agreement and drilling facility credit agreement with NBS Holding LLC.
claims.source_outlet: Petroleum News (Kay Cashman)
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: DNR issued a notice of default and cure demand for the Cosmopolitan Unit on May 23rd, 2025.
claims.verbatim: On May 23, 2025, DNR issued a notice of default and cure demand (default notice) for the Cosmopolitan Unit.
claims.source_outlet: Petroleum News (Kay Cashman)

claims.claim: Section 2103 adds a section 224 to the Federal Power Act requiring the Secretary of Energy to study electric transmission capacity constraints and congestion within 1 year of enactment and every 3 years after.
claims.verbatim: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this section and every 3 years thereafter, the Secretary of Energy ... shall conduct a study of electric transmission capacity constraints and congestion.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: New Federal Power Act section 224(d), titled Alaska, requires the Secretary of Energy to consider intrastate transmission constraints and congestion within Alaska in consultation with the State of Alaska and affected Indian Tribes.
claims.verbatim: (d) Alaska.--The Secretary-- (1) shall, in consultation with the State of Alaska and affected Indian Tribes, consider any intrastate transmission capacity constraints and congestion within the State of Alaska in the study under subsection (a)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Under section 224(d), the Secretary may identify an Alaska area as transmission-constrained or congested only subject to the approval of the Regulatory Commission of Alaska.
claims.value: subject to the approval of the Regulatory Commission of Alaska
claims.verbatim: may, subject to the approval of the Regulatory Commission of Alaska, identify any geographic area in the State of Alaska that-- (A) is experiencing electric energy transmission capacity constraints or congestion that adversely affects consumers; or (B) is expected to experience such energy transmission capacity constraints or congestion.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: For the rest of the country, section 224(b)(3) lets the Secretary identify constrained or congested areas after considering comments, with no state commission approval step.
claims.verbatim: the Secretary may identify in a report issued under paragraph (1) any geographic area that-- (A) is experiencing electric energy transmission capacity constraints or congestion that adversely affects consumers
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl. Comparison of 224(b)(3) with 224(d)(2); the approval clause appears only in (d).

claims.claim: New Federal Power Act section 229 is titled Ratepayer protection with respect to data centers.
claims.verbatim: SEC. 229. RATEPAYER PROTECTION WITH RESPECT TO DATA CENTERS.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229 defines a computational load site as buildings at a single location that primarily contain IT infrastructure used for software services, artificial intelligence training, deployment and delivery, cryptocurrency mining or other data center computation.
claims.value: artificial intelligence training, deployment, and delivery
claims.verbatim: primarily contain information technology infrastructure used for-- (i) creating, executing, and delivering software applications and services; (ii) artificial intelligence training, deployment, and delivery; (iii) cryptocurrency mining; or (iv) other computational activities at a data center.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229(b)(1), headed No subsidy of data centers, bars allocating any portion of the retail incremental cost of serving a computational load site to any other customer.
claims.verbatim: No subsidy of data centers.--No portion of the retail incremental cost may be allocated to, or recovered in the rates of, any customer other than a computational load owner or a computational load operator.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229 defines retail incremental cost as the costs that would be avoided had the data center not been served, including generation, storage, transmission and distribution.
claims.verbatim: costs that would be avoided had a specific computational load owner or computational load operator not been served by an electric utility, including all costs to construct, own, and operate power generation or storage resources and electric transmission and distribution services
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229(b)(3) requires recovery of the full retail incremental cost to continue even if the data center ends its contract or stops buying power early.
claims.verbatim: such recovery shall continue notwithstanding the termination by the computational load owner or computational load operator of a contract
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229(b)(4) requires a utility to obtain reasonable financial assurances from the data center before building or upgrading facilities to serve it.
claims.verbatim: an electric utility shall require the computational load owner or computational load operator to provide reasonable financial assurances or contributions sufficient to cover the expected cost
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229(d) lets a State treat data center owners and operators as a separate class of retail electric service with less favorable rates and priorities than other large loads.
claims.verbatim: A State may-- (1) treat computational load owners and computational load operators as a separate class of retail electric service; and (2) establish rates, charges, terms, conditions, and interconnection or service priorities ... that are less favorable than, those applicable to other large industrial, manufacturing, or commercial loads.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229 says a State includes an applicable State commission or other State authority over retail electric service.
claims.verbatim: The term `State' includes-- (A) an applicable State commission; and (B) any other State authority with jurisdiction over retail electric service.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229(c)(1)(D) lets a State condition service to a data center on the data center procuring or building enough new generation to serve its own demand.
claims.verbatim: condition the provision of retail electric service to a computational load site on the procurement, construction, or contracting by the computational load owner or computational load operator for new generation resources sufficient to serve the demand of the computational load site
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229(f) applies the cost floor and the state powers to data centers that interconnect on or after enactment.
claims.verbatim: Subsections (b) and (c) apply to any computational load site that interconnects on or after the date of enactment of this section.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229(e) says nothing in it expands or diminishes the jurisdiction of FERC or any State.
claims.verbatim: Nothing in this section expands or diminishes the jurisdiction of the Commission or any State
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 229 as passed by the Senate sets no megawatt threshold in its definition of a computational load site.
claims.verbatim: The term `computational load site' means 1 or more buildings, structures, or installations at a single location that primarily contain information technology infrastructure
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl. Read the whole of section 229 (lines 6676 to 6880 of the text); no MW figure in the definition. Compare S. 5653 as introduced (20 MW covered load).

claims.claim: Section 2114 requires the Energy Information Administration to revise Form 861 to separately include information from computational load sites before the first April 1st after enactment.
claims.verbatim: the Administrator of the Energy Information Administration shall revise Form 861 (or any successor form) of the Energy Information Administration to separately include information from computational load sites.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 2107 finds it is United States policy that computational load owners and operators bear the full cost of the electric service and infrastructure built to serve them.
claims.verbatim: it is the policy of the United States that computational load owners and computational load operators bear the full cost of any electric service that they require and the full cost of any infrastructure built to serve them
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: Section 2107 requires FERC to issue a final rule on transmission rates for computational load customers within 1 year of its proposed rule.
claims.verbatim: Not later than 1 year after the date on which the notice of proposed rulemaking described in subparagraph (A)(ii) is issued, the Commission shall issue a final rule
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.

claims.claim: The Senate's engrossed amendment to H.R. 2347 is dated November 19th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: In the Senate of the United States, November 19, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Government Publishing Office, H.R. 2347 Engrossed Amendment Senate (EAS)
claims.notes: Showrunner read of the full text via curl.
